5445.t: From Proto-Hellenic *Dzéus (whence Mycenaean Greek 𐀇𐀺 (di-wo /⁠diwos⁠/)), from Proto-Indo-European *dyḗws. Cognate with Sanskrit द्यौस् (dyáus), Latin deus and Iovis (and *Iu- in Iuppiter), Old English Tīw, Hittite 𒅆𒍑 (sius).

5457.t: From πέτρος (pétros, “stone, rock”), related to πέτρα (pétra).

5404.t: Seems to be a contraction of an original *ὀποσάρα (*oposára), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁epi (“on, at”) (whence ἐπί (epĭ́)) + *(s)h₁ósr̥, a variant of *(s)h₁ésō (“harvest season”), from *(s)h₁es- (“crop, harvest”); the exact formation *(s)h₁ósr̥ is found…

5453.t: From the monophthongisation of the non-Attic diphthong ⟨ωυ⟩ to ⟨ω⟩ in earlier Μωυσῆς (Mōusês, disyllabic), which was likely formed under Ionic influence, from Biblical Hebrew מֹשֶׁה (mōšê).

5419.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ugrós, from Proto-Indo-European *wegʷ- (“wet, moist”). Cognate with Latin ūvidus.

5464.t: From σῴζω (sōízō, “save”) + πατήρ (pătḗr, “father”), literally “savior of the father.” Compare Σωσικράτης (Sōsĭkrắtēs) / Σωκράτης (Sōkrắtēs, “Socrates”), Σωσικλείδης (Sōsĭkleídēs) / Σωκλείδης (Sōkleídēs, “Socleides”).

5458.t: Related to σήρ (sḗr, “silkworm”) but otherwise uncertain. Possibly ultimately from Old Chinese 絲 (*sə, “silk”).

5475.t: Uncertain. Beekes mentions that derivation from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eysd- (“to laud, honour”) + *-ōs, though semantically attractive, is formally difficult, as the expected form would be **αἰζώς (**aizṓs).

5416.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sór-mos (compare Old Armenian որմ (orm, “wall, fence”)), from *ser- (“to bind”). Cognate with Ancient Greek εἴρω (eírō, “to tie, fasten”), Latin serō (“to bind”), Proto-Germanic *sarwą (“armour”).

5467.t: From Hebrew צָרְפַת (ṣārĕp̄aṯ) or a cognate in a different Semitic language.

5400.t: According to Beekes, the term derives from the root Proto-Indo-European *h₃elh₁- with a k-enlargement. For comparison, see terms such as ἐρύκω (erúkō).

5435.t: Of uncertain origin. Perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *(s)rowpos (“accumulated filth”) and cognate with Proto-Slavic *strupъ (“scab”).

5433.t: Clear morphological cognates lacking outside Greek. The traditional comparison with Sanskrit वृश्चति (vṛścati, “to hew, cleave”) is not accepted by Beekes.

5431.t: From ῥάπτω (rháptō, “to sew”) + -ις (-ĭs). Compare typologically Latin sūbula, Proto-Slavic *šidlo (< Proto-Indo-European *syewH- + *-dʰlom).

5486.t: Unknown. According to Beekes the word is perhaps Pre-Greek, in view of the variation -λλ-/-λ-.

5436.t: From Proto-Indo-European *wroh₁ǵ-s, derivative of *wreh₁ǵ- (“to break, tear”), the same root of ῥήγνυμι (rhḗgnumi, “to break”).

5434.t: According to Beekes, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *rewH- (“to draw”) and related to ἐρύω (erúō, “to draw, tear”), ῥυμός (rhumós, “pole of a chariot”) and ῥυτά (rhutá, “reins”).

5413.t: Etymology tree Pre-Greekbor.? Ancient Greek ὄνος (ónos) Proto-Indo-European *h₂eǵ-? Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵros Proto-Indo-European *-yós Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵr̥yos Ancient Greek ἄγριος (ắgrĭos) Ancient Greek ὄναγρος From ὄνος (ónos, “ass, donkey”)…

5440.t: Borrowed from Old Persian *Bagāvahyah, from 𐏎 (BG /⁠bagaʰ⁠/, “god”) + *vahyah (“better”). Cognate with Imperial Aramaic 𐡁𐡂𐡅𐡄𐡉 (bgwhy).

5494.t: A reduplicated formation from the zero grade of Proto-Indo-European *gʷeh₂- (“to step, go”) with -άζω (-ázō), functioning as a factitive (causative) present meaning “to make or cause to go”.

5430.t: Possibly from ῥέπω (rhépō, “to let fall, drop, decline, descend”) + -ίζω (-ízō); related to ῥαπίς (rhapís), ῥάβδος (rhábdos, “rod, staff”).

5408.t: From ὅλος (hólos, “whole”) + an element *σχερός (*skherós, “row”), the latter formed from a zero-grade of Proto-Indo-European *seǵʰ- (“to hold, have”), + -ής (-ḗs). See also ἐπισχερώ (episkherṓ, “in a row”).

5405.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂ogʰléyeti, from *h₂egʰ- (“to be upset, afraid”). By surface analysis, ὄχλος (ókhlos) + -έω (-éō).
